name: tear
title: Tear
description: A sheet of paper drops over the page and is torn in two. A real cloth simulation, rendered with three.js. GSAP + three.
docs:
Wrap your layout with the transition. This is the only step:

  // app/layout.tsx
  import { TearTransition } from "@/components/tear"

  export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
    return (
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <TearTransition>{children}</TearTransition>
        </body>
      </html>
    )
  }

Your existing <Link>s are intercepted automatically.

A sheet of paper drops over the page, the route swaps behind it, and the sheet
is torn in two: a jagged seam races down while the halves are pulled apart,
then they come free and fall out of frame. The paper is a real cloth
simulation stepped at a fixed 120Hz, and no two tears are alike. Rendered
with three.js, which this component installs — it is the one transition in
the set that carries a real dependency for its drawing, about 130KB gzipped.
The WebGL context is created while the page is idle; browsers without WebGL
navigate plainly.

cols sets the mesh density, stiffness how much the paper resists bending,
gravity how fast the halves fall, pull how hard they are pulled apart, jag
how rough the seam is, duration how long the tear takes.

Colour: paper="chalk" (default), "kraft", "newsprint" or "ink" (black). For
anything else pass paper="custom" and set --tear-paper in
components/transitions.css.

Note: browser back/forward is not animated, and the route does not start
loading until the leave phase finishes (~0.85s).
